mechanism_narrative: A low federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) compresses discount rates for equity valuation, generating positive S&P 500 forward returns over 20 trading days. The signal is continuously active and level-dependent.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of periods when FEDFUNDS is below 0.5%, or the Rank IC between FEDFUNDS and 20-day returns is below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A rising unemployment rate (UNRATE) above 5.0% signals economic weakness, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day returns are positive in more than 60% of periods when UNRATE > 5.0%, or the Rank IC between UNRATE and 5-day returns is below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous growth in housing starts (HOUST) and real consumption (RSAFS) indicates robust consumer demand, driving positive S&P 500 returns over 60 trading days through stronger corporate earnings.
failure_condition: The interaction term between HOUST and RSAFS (product of z-scores) has a negative Rank IC over any 3-year window, or the average 60-day return is negative when both series are above their 12-month moving averages.

mechanism_narrative: During a monetary tightening cycle (FEDFUNDS > 4.0% and rising for 3 months), the S&P 500 experiences negative forward returns over 20 trading days due to higher discount rates.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of periods when FEDFUNDS > 4.0% and rising for 3 months, or the Rank IC between FEDFUNDS (in tightening regime) and 20-day returns is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in industrial production (INDPRO) below 95.0 signals manufacturing contraction, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of periods when INDPRO < 95.0, or the Rank IC between INDPRO and 20-day returns is below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: High housing starts (HOUST > 700.0) indicate strong consumer demand, generating positive S&P 500 returns over 5 trading days through immediate market sentiment.
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day returns are negative in more than 60% of periods when HOUST > 700.0, or the Rank IC between HOUST and 5-day returns is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: In a high-unemployment regime (UNRATE > 7.0%), the S&P 500 produces negative forward returns over 20 trading days due to recessionary fears and reduced corporate investment.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of periods when UNRATE > 7.0%, or the Rank IC between UNRATE and 20-day returns is below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: Persistent inflation (CPIAUCSL annual change > 3.0%) signals central bank hawkishness, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over 60 trading days as real rates rise.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are positive in more than 60% of periods when CPIAUCSL annual change > 3.0%, or the Rank IC between CPIAUCSL (annual change) and 60-day returns is below 0.03.
